evidence: src/infrastructure/persistence/InMemoryOrderRepository.ts doc comment: 'Stores snapshots rather than live entities, so changes only become visible once a use case explicitly saves them.'
src/infrastructure/persistence/InMemoryProductRepository.ts has the identical doc comment, so the same invariant is declared twice
InMemoryOrderRepository.save: this.records.set(order.id, structuredClone(order.toSnapshot())); stores a deep-copied snapshot
InMemoryProductRepository.save: this.records.set(product.id, product.toSnapshot()); stores the snapshot without cloning, so isolation depends on how deep toSnapshot copies
Both classes repeat the same private readonly records = new Map<string, Snapshot>() plus findById/findAll restore logic, with no shared abstraction to enforce the snapshot rule in one place
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files have the same job: in-memory, snapshot-based persistence that implements domain repository interfaces. The problem is the storage invariant written in each file's doc comment: "changes only become visible once a use case explicitly saves them." Each file enforces it with its own copy of the code, and the two copies have already drifted apart. InMemoryOrderRepository.save stores structuredClone(order.toSnapshot()), a deep copy, so later changes to the entity can't reach the stored record. InMemoryProductRepository.save stores product.toSnapshot() as-is. If ProductSnapshot holds nested objects or arrays shared with the live entity, changes leak into storage without a save, which breaks the guarantee the comment makes. Because the rule is duplicated instead of living in one shared place (for example a generic snapshot store or base class that does the cloning), the module has two different meanings of "snapshot". The duplicated findById/findAll restore logic shows the same missing shared piece. I can't see Product.toSnapshot, so I can't confirm a real leak, which keeps my confidence moderate. The divergence is still a case of the same invariant being duplicated and applied inconsistently.

violations.message: save() stores product.toSnapshot() without the structuredClone that InMemoryOrderRepository uses. The module's shared snapshot-isolation rule ('changes only become visible once ... saved') is copied into each file and applied differently, so nested snapshot state may stay shared with the live Product.

Has its own copy of the snapshot-storage rule (doc comment, Map-of-snapshots, clone-on-save, restore-on-read) instead of sharing one module abstraction with InMemoryProductRepository. That duplication is why the two repositories have drifted apart.
